sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Carrollton, GA?
sections.html:
Carrollton sellers can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take a cash offer for the house in its current condition. The choice usually comes down to how much time you have, what the house needs, and whether tenants or a co-owner complicate the sale.

  • An agent listing exposes the house to the most buyers but adds showings, inspection requests and a lender's timeline.
  • A sale by owner removes the listing agent but leaves pricing, paperwork and negotiation with you.
  • An as-is cash sale limits steps and repairs, at a price that usually sits below a polished retail listing.

Renters outnumber owners in Carrollton, which shapes the local market. According to the Census Bureau, 41.0 percent of housing units here are owner-occupied for 2020-2024, and 73.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

sections.h2: How does the University of West Georgia shape Carrollton?
sections.html:
The University of West Georgia sits on the western side of Carrollton, and its history is tied to the city's growth. The state's 1906 Perry Act created agricultural and mechanical schools in each congressional district, and in 1907 the trustees bought the 275-acre Bluford Sharp farm west of Carrollton for $9,625 as the Fourth District A&M School site. The school opened in January 1908.

On April 15, 1933, the Board of Regents chose the Carrollton campus for a new junior college named West Georgia College. It became the State University of West Georgia in 1996 and the University of West Georgia on January 12, 2005, according to the university library's timeline. One small piece of town history shows how closely the two are linked: the campus chapel was built in 1893 in downtown Carrollton and moved to the university grounds in 1964.

Not every Carrollton house sits in a college neighborhood, so ask a local agent or investor how far from campus your street is before you assume that demand reaches you.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Carrollton compared with the U.S.?
sections.html:
Carrollton's estimated population is 27,925 as of July 1, 2025, up 4.5 percent from the April 2020 estimates base, and the city covers 22.41 square miles of land. The Census Bureau's figures below are for 2020-2024 unless noted.

Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $1,590 in Carrollton against $1,963 nationally, and 88.5 percent of households have a broadband subscription. Poverty is 25.4 percent, so affordability is a live issue for local buyers, and a house that needs work may lose more value in a retail sale than the repair would cost.

sections.h2: Which school district serves Carrollton houses?
sections.html:
Carrollton City Schools operates its own district. It describes four schools on one 130-acre campus: Carrollton Elementary, Carrollton Upper Elementary, Carrollton Middle School and Carrollton High, with the district office at 106 Trojan Drive.

Which system serves a given address depends on whether the house is inside the city limits, so confirm the district for your exact address with the school system before you quote it in a listing. Buyers with children often ask this first, and an accurate answer saves time with a serious buyer.

sections.h2: Do you need a license to rent out a Carrollton house short term?
sections.html:
Yes. Carrollton adopted a short-term rental article in July 2025 as Chapter 18, Article VI of its code of ordinances. A short-term rental is a dwelling or part of one rented for lodging for no more than 30 consecutive days.

  • An annual license is required, with a non-refundable application fee of $500 filed with Community Development.
  • Occupancy is limited to two adults per bedroom and parking to one vehicle per bedroom, all on paved surfaces and none on the street.
  • No outside signage is allowed, and the license number must appear on every online listing.
  • Three convictions or judgments for code violations lead to revocation for 12 consecutive months.
  • An appeal of a denial, suspension or revocation goes in writing to the Mayor and City Council within 30 calendar days.

Short-term rentals are also subject to the hotel-motel tax. A license is tied to the owner and the address and cannot be transferred, so a buyer who plans to run the house as a rental must apply for their own. Call the city at 770-830-2000 with questions on licensing, building permits or code enforcement.

sections.h2: How do Carroll County assessments and tax bills affect a Carrollton sale?
sections.html:
Carroll County assesses and bills Carrollton property. The county's property tax page explains that the assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value as of January 1, and that one mill equals $1.00 per $1,000 of assessed value. Several bodies set rates: the county commissioners for county operations, the board of education for schools, and the state, which can levy no more than one quarter of a mill.

Appeals of value go first to the Board of Tax Assessors and then, if needed, to the County Board of Equalization, which the grand jury appoints. Arbitration is available in place of the Board of Equalization at the taxpayer's choice when the appeal is filed. Georgia assessment notices carry a 45-day appeal window, so use the date printed on your own notice. In Carroll County, returns and homestead exemption applications go through the Board of Assessors, while the tax commissioner bills and collects: call 770-830-5843 about calculations, late payments and interest.

Georgia's real estate transfer tax also applies on the sale. The Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each further $100 or fraction, with the seller liable unless the contract shifts it to the buyer. Ask the clerk of Carroll County Superior Court about any exemption question.

faqs.q: What is the population of Carrollton, GA?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 27,925 residents as of July 1, 2025. The April 2020 census count was 26,738 and the 2010 count was 24,388.

faqs.q: Does Carrollton require a license for Airbnb-style rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's short-term rental article requires an annual license with a $500 non-refundable application fee for stays of 30 consecutive days or fewer, and the license cannot be transferred to a new owner.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Carrollton, Georgia?
faqs.a: Carroll County does. The Board of Tax Assessors sets values and the county tax commissioner prepares and mails the bills, collects payments and answers questions at 770-830-5843.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Carrollton house with tenants in place?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer purchasing as-is can take a house with tenants, subject to the lease. Tell any buyer about the lease terms early, and ask your closing attorney how deposits and rent are handled at closing.
